IsoformicExperiment: Transcript, Gene and Exon Level Data in One Object

Source: R/IsoformicExperiment-class.R
IsoformicExperiment.Rd

IsoformicExperiment is an S7 class modelled after SummarizedExperiment, but organised around transcriptomic diversity: the same samples are described at three levels that are kept consistent by construction.

  • Transcript level: assays are numeric matrices with transcript IDs as row names and sample IDs as column names (for example abundance, counts, length). All assays share the same dimnames.

  • Gene level: gene assays are derived from the transcript assays by summing the isoforms of each gene (abundance-weighted means for length), cached, and can be overridden with gene_assays<-.

  • Exon level: exon structures come from the annotation and are available through annot_data_exons(), exon_table() and exon_diversity().

Annotation is never copied into the object. The annot_path property points to an annotation directory of Parquet files created by prepare_isoformic_annotation() (a GFF3/GTF file is accepted and converted on the fly). Tables are read with DuckDB on first access and cached in memory keyed by file path, size and modification time, so a re-created annotation is picked up automatically and several objects sharing one annotation share one copy of the tables.

Derived results (gene assays, row data, isoform fractions, ORFs, transcript features and productivity classes) are cached per object in the .cache environment, keyed by a hash of their inputs, and therefore survive copies but never go stale. See clear_cache().

Objects persist to disk as a directory of Parquet files with write_isoformic() and are restored with read_isoformic().

Usage

IsoformicExperiment(
  experiment_name = NULL,
  annot_path = NULL,
  assays = list(),
  col_data = NULL,
  gene_assays = list(),
  dea = list(),
  gsea = list(),
  metadata = list(),
  data_path = NULL,
  tx_type_palette = NULL
)

Arguments

experiment_name

Single string naming the experiment; a random name is generated when NULL.

annot_path

Annotation directory or GFF3/GTF file.

assays

Named list of transcript-level matrices (or data frames with a transcript_id column).

col_data

Data frame of sample metadata with a sample_id column (or sample IDs as row names / first column). NULL builds it from the column names of the assays.

gene_assays

Optional named list of gene-level matrices.

dea

Optional list of differential expression results.

gsea

Optional named list of enrichment results.

metadata

Optional named list of free-form metadata.

data_path

Optional on-disk location of the experiment.

tx_type_palette

Optional named colour vector per transcript type.

Value

An IsoformicExperiment object.

Properties

experiment_name

Single string. Generated when not supplied.

annot_path

Path to the annotation directory, or NULL for an empty object.

data_path

Directory the object was written to or read from (see write_isoformic()), or NULL.

assays

Named list of transcript-level matrices.

gene_assays

Named list of gene-level matrices. Derived from assays when not set explicitly.

col_data

Tibble of sample metadata; its sample_id column matches the assay column names.

dea

List with differential expression results: det (transcripts), deg (genes) and cutoffs, and the uncertainty tables of add_uncertainty(). Use de_tx<- and de_gene<- to set the results.

gsea

Named list of enrichment result tables.

metadata

Free-form named list.

annot_metadata

Named list describing the annotation source, read from the annotation directory unless set explicitly.

tx_type_palette

Named character vector of colours per transcript type, used by all plots. Defaults to tx_type_palette().

annot_data_transcripts, annot_data_genes, annot_data_exons

Read-only, cached annotation tables.

Subsetting

x[i, j] keeps the transcripts i and the samples j, given as IDs, positions or logical vectors; a missing i or j keeps all of them, and the subset must hold at least one transcript and one sample. Everything stored by transcript or by sample follows: the assays, the sample table, stored gene assays (the genes of the kept transcripts) and the inferential replicates in x@metadata$inf_reps. The uncertainty tables of add_uncertainty() are restricted to the kept transcripts (a collapsed ambiguity group stays only with all its members); when samples are dropped they are not recomputed, and a message says so. Differential expression and enrichment results are kept as they are.

The inferential replicates are not copied: the metadata$inf_reps of a subset holds the draws of x and a selection attribute, a list with the IDs of the kept transcripts and samples. The functions of the package (and inferential_replicates_table()) read the draws through that selection, and write_isoformic() writes only the selected rows and columns, so the results are those of a copy of the kept draws, while the memory of a subset does not grow with the draws. The trade-off: the draws of x (every transcript and sample) stay in memory as long as a subset made from it exists, even after x itself is removed, and they go with every serialised copy of the subset: saveRDS(), serialize() and the objects sent to parallel workers that do not share memory (such as future or mirai workers) carry every transcript and sample of the draws of x, while write_isoformic() writes only the selected ones. Code that indexes the matrices of metadata$inf_reps directly sees the draws of x. A list operation on metadata$inf_reps (such as lapply() or [) drops the selection attribute and returns the draws of x: the functions that take the object still read only its kept transcripts and samples, while code that gets only the list, such as inferential_replicates_table() without its x argument, reads every transcript and sample of x. When no kept transcript has draws, the subset keeps only the replicate moments (with zero-row draws), so that scale_counts() and inferential_overdispersion() still work, but the functions that need the draws treat it as an object without inferential replicates; without moments, metadata$inf_reps is NULL. To replace the draws by plain matrices of the kept draws (and free those of x), write the subset with write_isoformic() and read it back; to drop them, set metadata$inf_reps <- NULL. To compare two groups of a larger object, pass levels to the function instead of subsetting: the samples of the other groups are ignored. A subset with other transcripts starts with an empty cache of derived tables (the transcript annotation join is shared).

See also

example_isoformic() for a ready-made object, read_salmon() and as_isoformic() to create one from quantifications, IsoformicExperiment-accessors for the accessor generics.

Examples

iso <- example_isoformic()
iso
#> <IsoformicExperiment> pe_placenta_example
#>   annotation : gencode_v50_example_subset (69 genes, 1,914 transcripts, 18,656 exons)
#>   samples    : 25 [condition]
#>   transcripts: 1,911 assayed from 69 genes
#>   assays     : abundance, counts
#>   gene assays: derived from transcript assays on demand
#>   DE results : det (710 transcripts), deg (69 genes)
dim(iso)
#> [1] 1911   25
assay_names(iso)
#> [1] "abundance" "counts"

# Subset like a SummarizedExperiment. Stored gene assays, inferential
# replicates and uncertainty tables follow the transcripts and samples kept
iso[1:10, c("SRR11498039", "SRR11498063")]
#> <IsoformicExperiment> pe_placenta_example
#>   annotation : gencode_v50_example_subset (69 genes, 1,914 transcripts, 18,656 exons)
#>   samples    : 2 [condition]
#>   transcripts: 10 assayed from 1 genes
#>   assays     : abundance, counts
#>   gene assays: derived from transcript assays on demand
#>   DE results : det (710 transcripts), deg (69 genes)

# Build one from matrices
annot <- system.file("extdata", "example_experiment", "annotation", package = "isoformic")
tpm <- tx_assay(iso, "abundance")[1:5, 1:3]
small <- IsoformicExperiment(
  experiment_name = "tiny",
  annot_path = annot,
  assays = list(abundance = tpm),
  col_data = data.frame(sample_id = colnames(tpm), condition = c("a", "a", "b"))
)
small
#> <IsoformicExperiment> tiny
#>   annotation : gencode_v50_example_subset (69 genes, 1,914 transcripts, 18,656 exons)
#>   samples    : 3 [condition]
#>   transcripts: 5 assayed from 1 genes
#>   assays     : abundance
#>   gene assays: derived from transcript assays on demand
#>   DE results : <none>
